summary: Well‑executed preregistered paired experiment with comprehensive artifact grounding. The manuscript demonstrates that runtime verifier feedback with a bounded repair (guarded) produced a small but statistically supported increase in safe end‑to‑end completions versus a static post‑hoc verifier on a deterministic synthetic/emulated NetOps corpus. Preregistration, deterministic execution logs, contingency counts, bootstrap CI recomputation for the sensitivity encoding, and a detailed Disclosure Statement are all present in the archived artifacts. Major methodological limitations (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model, synthetic/emulated scope, and an unexecuted preregistered latency diagnostic) are disclosed.
optional_revisions: Reduce provenance‑heavy inline text outside the mandatory Disclosure Statement to improve narrative readability (move long provenance lists to the archived artifact bundle references).

Explicitly name the analysis executor binary/release or exact implementation used for the exact McNemar test and for bootstrap resampling (the artifacts record 'paired_binary_analysis_v1'—cite that executor and its version in Methods).

Add one concise sentence in the Methods summarizing how the shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation=false) were implemented in code (artifact path and brief mapping to the task_manifest entry) to make construct validity immediately clear to readers unfamiliar with the artifact layout.
